answer: Under standard plans, you have 30 days from the date of discharge to submit a main reimbursement claim [1], [2]. However, for Aurora Group Health corporate plans, the submission deadline is extended to 60 days from discharge [5]. (Note that archived 2024 rules previously listed a 15-day limit [3].)

The room rent limit on the Silver plan is 2% of the sum insured per day [3], [4]. If a room exceeding this limit is occupied, proportionate deduction applies to reduce all associated hospital charges in the same proportion [5].
No, maternity is not covered on the Bronze plan at any sum insured [1], [2]. Maternity cover is only available on the Silver, Gold, and Platinum plans [1].

The waiting period for pre-existing diseases on standard retail plans is 36 months, unless explicitly waived in writing by Aurora on the policy schedule [3], [5]. However, under the Aurora Senior Care plan for individuals aged 60 and above, the waiting period for pre-existing diseases is reduced to 24 months [5].
The grace period for an annual policy is 30 days from the renewal due date [1], [5]. Renewing within this period preserves continuity benefits such as waiting periods and no-claim bonuses [3].

As of 1 April 2026, Aurora's network covers 11,400 hospitals across 780 towns [1]. Because hospitals join and leave the network continuously, this figure is indicative, and the authoritative list is maintained in the Aurora app and portal hospital locator [1].

The no-claim bonus on the Aurora Gold plan is 25% of the base sum insured per claim-free year, accumulating up to a maximum of 100% [1], [5]. If a claim is made, the accumulated bonus is not reduced; it simply stops accumulating for that specific year [1].
No, you cannot claim for IVF treatment. According to the policy, infertility, assisted reproduction, and IVF are listed under permanent treatment-related exclusions [1].
The cataract surgery sub-limit on the Aurora Gold plan is ₹75,000 per eye [1].

If an internal outcome is unsatisfactory, you can first escalate to Aurora's Grievance Redressal Officer (GRO) [2]. If Aurora's final response is unsatisfactory, or if they have not responded within 30 days of the original complaint, you can approach the Insurance Ombudsman for your region [1].

Across all plans, there is road ambulance cover of ₹5,000 per hospitalisation [1]. Additionally, under the Aurora Gold plan, air ambulance is covered up to ₹2,50,000 per policy year within India with prior authorisation [5].

Yes, in-patient treatment for mental illness is covered on the same terms as physical illness, as mandated by the Mental Healthcare Act 2017 [1]. The coverage is subject to a 30-day initial waiting period, with no separate waiting period required [1].

The free-look period is the window in which a new policyholder can return or cancel a policy for a refund [2, 3]. It lasts for 15 days from the receipt of the policy document, or 30 days if the policy was sold through distance marketing [1, 2]. If cancelled within this timeframe, the policyholder receives a refund of the premium minus the proportionate risk premium for the period of cover, medical examination costs, and stamp duty [2].
You get 150 wellness points per year for completing an annual health check-up [1].

A day-care procedure is a procedure that requires less than 24 hours of hospitalisation due to technological advances, making it payable despite the general 24-hour admission requirement [3]. Out-patient treatment is not considered a day-care procedure [3].
For an emergency admission under the cashless route, the hospital must notify Aurora within 24 hours of admission [1], [5].
No, Aurora does not use a Third Party Administrator (TPA) [1]. Instead, Aurora administers its own claims directly [1].
To qualify as a hospital, a facility must have at least 10 in-patient beds in towns with a population below 10 lakh [1]. In all other locations, it must have at least 15 in-patient beds [1].

No, everything will not be fully paid. Under the Silver plan with a ₹5,00,000 sum insured, the room-rent limit is 2% of the sum insured, which is ₹10,000 per day [1], [2]. Because taking a room at ₹15,000 per day exceeds this limit, a proportionate deduction based on an eligibility ratio of 0.667 will apply to your claim, reducing the total amount payable [1], [5].

You can add a dependent parent under the Silver plan (at an extra premium), Gold plan, or Platinum plan, but not under the Bronze plan [1]. When you add her, your policy premium will be determined by the age of the eldest member covered, which often results in a higher cost than purchasing an individual senior-citizen policy for her [4].

Your served waiting period will carry over, but only up to the sum insured of your previous policy, including any accrued no-claim bonus [1], [2]. Any incremental increase or excess in the sum insured will be subject to fresh waiting periods on that additional amount [1], [2].

While your newborn is covered automatically for the first 90 days from birth under the maternity limit [2], you must inform Aurora within 90 days of birth to add the baby as a dependent to continue coverage beyond 90 days with guaranteed-issue terms [1]. Additionally, if you are filing a reimbursement claim for the delivery, you must submit the claim within 30 days of discharge and post-hospitalisation bills within 15 days of the post-hospitalisation period ending [3].

Under the Aurora Silver plan, having a claim reduces your accumulated no-claim bonus by 10 percentage points [1]. The claim does not reset your bonus to zero [1].
Under the Gold plan, the maternity benefit limit for a caesarean section is ₹1,00,000 [1]. If the hospital bills ₹1,60,000, your out-of-pocket cost would be ₹60,000 [1].

No, knee joint replacement is not covered immediately under standard circumstances, as it is subject to a 24-month waiting period [1], [5]. However, if the knee replacement is required following an accident, it is covered immediately from day one [1], [2], [5].

Total discounts are capped at 30% of the base premium [1]. However, the wellness discount of up to 15% is applied last, after the cap, and is the only discount that may exceed the 30% limit [1], [3], [5].

Cashless access is not permitted at an excluded provider and will be denied at pre-authorisation [2], [3], [4]. Your only option is to seek reimbursement, which requires pre-approval [3], and the claim is payable only if the admission was a genuine emergency where no alternative facility was reachable [1].

The deadline to respond to an Aurora query depends on the type of claim:

* For general reimbursement claims, you have **45 days** from the date of the query to respond, after which the claim is closed [2], [5].
* For motor insurance claims, you have **30 days** from the date of the query [4].

According to current guidelines, a planned cashless admission must be notified at least 72 hours before admission [2], [3]. However, there is a conflict with archived rules, which state the notification deadline is 48 hours before admission [1].

Aurora settles or rejects a complete reimbursement claim within 15 working days of receiving the last required document, with the clock restarting if a query is raised and the required document is supplied [1], [2]. In contrast, archived 2024 rules previously set the reimbursement settlement timeline at 30 days from the last document [3].
The Aurora Gold plan has no co-payment across all ages [1]. In addition, the Aurora Silver plan has no co-payment for claims when the eldest insured member is below age 60 [2].

Across the four Aurora health insurance plans, the pre-hospitalisation coverage windows are 30 days, 45 days, 60 days, and 90 days, respectively [1]. In comparison, the post-hospitalisation coverage windows for the four plans are 60 days, 90 days, 120 days, and 180 days, respectively [1].
You should consider the Gold plan, as it removes room-rent sub-limits [3] and provides coverage for dependent parents-in-law [1]. The Platinum plan also covers dependent parents-in-law [1].

Dental treatment and oral surgery are permanently excluded under Aurora indemnity plans, unless necessitated by an accidental injury requiring hospitalisation [2], [3]. Out-patient dental work is also specifically noted as an item not covered by any plan [1].

You will lose what you have built up—including accumulated no-claim bonuses and waiting period continuity—if you do not pay before the grace period expires [2], [3]. The grace period is 30 days for annual policies and 15 days for instalment policies [1], [5] (or 30 days for annual, half-yearly, and quarterly, and 15 days for monthly under life policies) [4]. Once this grace period lapses, the policy is treated as fresh, waiting periods restart, accumulated bonuses are lost, and fresh underwriting applies [2].

No, you are not finished. Denial of cashless is not a rejection of your claim [1]. Instead, you can file a claim for reimbursement under Route 2, which applies when cashless access is denied or when using non-network hospitals [3]. Note that if the hospital is an excluded provider, reimbursement is still possible but requires pre-approval [5].

Completing the quit-tobacco programme earns 200 wellness points per year [2]. These points can be used toward a renewal-premium discount, which converts at a rate of 1,000 points for a 5% discount (capped at 15%) [3].
